sources.entry: MacFanPro - Fan control for Apple Silicon Macs with a menu bar app, temperature-based profiles and a CLI. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/macfanpro/macfanpro) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]
MacFanPro - Fan control for Apple Silicon Macs with a menu bar app, smart temperature curves and a CLI.

summary.one_liner: MacFanPro is a free, open-source, native Swift menu bar app and CLI for monitoring temperatures and controlling fan speeds on Apple Silicon Macs with physical fans.
summary.what_it_does: MacFanPro shows CPU, GPU, memory, SSD and ambient temperatures and each fan's actual speed in a menu bar panel. It offers Smart, Silent, Balanced, Performance and Max profiles, plus a button to return to Apple's automatic control. A root-owned background service performs the privileged fan writes, and a watchdog hands the fans back to macOS if the app stops responding. The macfanpro CLI can set fan speeds, print status as JSON, and record sensor data to CSV. An optional calibration routine builds a temperature-to-fan lookup for Smart mode. The app is available in 18 interface languages.
use_cases: control fan speed on an Apple Silicon MacBook Pro
monitor Mac temperatures from the menu bar
record thermal sensor data during a workload
keep a Mac cooler during sustained compiling or rendering
replace a closed-source fan control utility with an open-source one
how_to_run: (set -o pipefail; curl -fsSL <installer URL> | bash)  # online installer; URL not preserved in the README text
notable: Native Swift menu bar app with no Electron and no Dock icon
Safety override at 95°C and a background thermal floor that works even when the app is closed
Watchdog returns fans to macOS if the app stops responding
Scriptable macfanpro CLI with JSON status and CSV recording
Smart profile uses temperature trend and optional calibration data
caveats: Requires an Apple Silicon Mac on macOS 14 or later with physical fans; Intel and fanless Macs such as MacBook Air are not supported
Release packages are ad-hoc signed and not yet notarized by Apple, so macOS may block the first launch
Installing the background service requires an administrator password
